state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: The authors suggest their theory points to a framework for encouraging weak-to-strong effects: find a neighborhood structure and student hypothesis class pair that expands, then pick the student that minimizes weak-label error while staying as robust as possible on the neighborhoods. Noting that both expansion and contrastive pretraining relate to spectral properties of the neighborhood graph, they ask whether weakly-supervised learning can be improved by imbuing the contrastive pretraining objective with knowledge of the pseudolabeler.
title: Open question: can pseudolabeler-aware contrastive pretraining improve weak-to-strong?
